Landscaping in Blaxland

Landscaping for Blaxland — the gateway to the Mountains. Fire-smart, low-maintenance gardens, turf, paving and clean-ups for busy families. 20% off this spring and summer.

Blaxland is the first town you reach climbing into the Blue Mountains from the Nepean plain, sitting lower and noticeably warmer than the suburbs further up. Frost is far less of an issue here, blocks are generally flatter and easier to work than the upper Mountains, and that opens up a lot of options for the family gardens that fill the area.

The catch in the lower Mountains is bushfire. Blaxland backs onto the national park and bushland corridors, so we design and maintain gardens with that front of mind — sensible plant choices and spacing near the house, defendable clear zones, and regular removal of leaf litter and yard fuel. A good-looking garden and a fire-smart one aren’t mutually exclusive, and that’s exactly what we aim for.

Most Blaxland homeowners want something that looks great without eating their weekends, so low-maintenance is the theme of a lot of our work here: hardy planting, clean paving and entertaining areas, quality turf or artificial grass, and tidy edges that stay looking good with minimal fuss. With Glenbrook, Warrimoo and Mount Riverview all close by, we’re across this end of the Mountains constantly.

What makes Blaxland different

  • Warmer, lower gateway suburb. The first town up from the plain — milder than the upper Mountains, with far less frost to plan around.
  • Flatter, family blocks. Generally gentler ground makes for straightforward builds, turf laying and entertaining areas.
  • Real bushfire exposure. Backing onto national park means fire-smart design, clear zones and regular fuel-load clean-ups matter here.
  • Busy-family gardens. Low-maintenance, good-looking outdoor spaces are what most Blaxland homes are after.

Blaxland FAQs

Common questions in Blaxland

Can you design a low-maintenance garden?

That’s most of what we do in Blaxland. Hardy planting, quality paving, turf or artificial grass and clean edges — a garden that looks great and gives you your weekends back.

How do you make a Blaxland garden fire-smart?

We use sensible plant choices and spacing near the house, keep defendable clear zones, and stay on top of leaf litter and yard fuel — so your garden looks good and is better prepared for fire season.

Is artificial grass a good option here?

Often, yes. For busy families or shaded, high-wear areas, premium artificial grass gives you a green lawn all year with none of the mowing — and we prep and install it properly so it stays put and drains well.
